subject: PromptCraft LangChain/LlamaIndex adapter & distributed tracing integration
messages:
From: Sarah Patel <sarah@promptcraft.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Devon Liu <devon@promptcraft.ai>
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Partnership inquiry — PromptCraft adapter + tracing integration

Hi Soojin,

Hope you’re well — I’m Sarah, Head of Partnerships at PromptCraft. We build a prompt-management and observability layer used by ISVs to track prompt provenance, prompt scoring, and prompt-level A/Bing. Over the last year customers have been asking for a first-class adapter into Redwood so we can:

- Route prompts through PromptCraft while keeping token accounting with Redwood
- Surface per-prompt tracing & latency metrics in our UI
- Provide a joint adapter for LangChain/LlamaIndex users to drop into their apps

Devon (cc’d) is our lead engineer on integrations. We put together a short spec (attached) that outlines the SDK hooks we need and a suggested mutual action plan. High level ask: are you interested in a co-marketed adapter + tracing contract that would make Redwood the preferred runtime for PromptCraft customers?

If yes, we’d love to kick off a scoping call next week. Proposed attendees: Partnerships, your SDK/Integrations PM, and an infra/serving engineer to discuss tracing format.

Best,
Sarah

[attachment: promptcraft_integration_spec_v1.pdf (PDF, 220KB)]
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Patel <sarah@promptcraft.ai>
Cc: Devon Liu <devon@promptcraft.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Partnership inquiry — PromptCraft adapter + tracing integration

Hi Sarah — thanks for the note and the spec. This is squarely in our partner/ISV playbook and we’re interested.

Quick items from my side before a scoping call:
1) Can you confirm the expected SLA profile for traced requests (p50/p95 goals) and whether you expect synchronous traces attached to every request or batched export?
2) Are you targeting both LangChain and LlamaIndex customers with the same adapter, or separate packages?
3) Will PromptCraft require any token-level proxying (where tokens pass through PromptCraft) or will you prefer a post-call telemetry export model?

I’ve looped in Marissa (product) to coordinate roadmap/marketing and Devon for engineering details. I’ll schedule a 45-minute scoping call for Thursday.

Soojin Lee
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Sarah Patel <sarah@promptcraft.ai>
Cc: Devon Liu <devon@promptcraft.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Partnership inquiry — PromptCraft adapter + tracing integration

Thanks, Soojin. Quick product note from our side: we see two priority integration patterns that customers expect:

- Inference-time SDK hook (preferred for prompt editing workflows): SDK intercepts prompt before send, allows PromptCraft to mutate/score, then hand back final prompt to Redwood runtime. This requires low-latency sync calls and careful token accounting.
- Post-hoc telemetry export: Redwood emits event batches with prompt hash, model id, latency and token counts. Lower coupling, easier to ship first.

For go-to-market we’d like a staged approach: pilot (post-hoc telemetry) -> adapter (LangChain/LlamaIndex shim) -> in-path prompt controls. Can you share a rough estimate for engineering time for the shim (LangChain + LlamaIndex) vs the in-path SDK?

Marissa Cole
Senior Product Manager, Integrations
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Devon Liu <devon@promptcraft.ai>, Sarah Patel <sarah@promptcraft.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Partnership inquiry — technical notes + tracing format

Hi all — I’m the runtime engineer on the serving side. A few technical constraints and a suggested implementation plan: 

Constraints:
- We avoid synchronous third-party hops in the token path by default because of tail latency and reliability impact.
- We can support synchronous enrichment if the partner provides a fallback cached response and adheres to our p95 latency SLOs.

Suggested plan (can be staged):
1) Pilot: Post-hoc telemetry export (recommended)
   - Redwood emits a telemetry event for each request: {timestamp, request_id, model, seq_len, prompt_hash, token_cost, p50/p95_latency}
   - Events batched every 15s to a partner endpoint or S3 export; we sign events with customer key
2) LangChain/LlamaIndex adapter (open-source repo)
   - Provide a small shim package that translates LangChain calls to our API and attaches prompt_hash for linking to telemetry
   - Provide examples for Python/JS
3) In-path SDK (optional stage)
   - If PromptCraft wants to mutate prompts inline we’ll require an opt-in integration and a fail-open policy; also need formal SLA and justification for the latency risk

Open questions for PromptCraft to answer prior to scoping:
- Preferred tracing format (OTLP/Jaeger/OpenTelemetry)?
- Expected retention window for prompt telemetry (days/months)?
- Are you comfortable receiving batched events vs. a streaming endpoint?

I attached a short adapter proposal (redwood_adapter-proposal.odt) with API examples and a sample LangChain shim.

Jonas Weber
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
jonas_weber@redwood.com

[attachment: redwood_adapter-proposal.odt (ODT, 95KB)]
From: Devon Liu <devon@promptcraft.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Patel <sarah@promptcraft.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Partnership inquiry — technical notes + tracing format

Thanks Jonas — really helpful. Answers inline: 

- Preferred tracing format: OpenTelemetry (OTLP) for telemetry exports; we can accept batched HTTP/JSON POSTs and will normalize.
- Retention: pilot customers typically keep prompt telemetry 30–90 days; enterprise customers request 365+ options.
- Batched events are fine for the first phase; we’d prefer webhooks only for alerting and real-time UX.
- LangChain and LlamaIndex: same adapter repo can expose two small helpers; we already have an internal shim for both.
- Synchronous in-path mutation: we prefer a non-blocking enrichment model: adapter returns a ‘suggestion’ that the app may apply; full blocking mutation would be reserved for advanced customers.

Links:
- SDK repo: https://github.com/promptcraft/sdk-langchain-adapter
- OTLP spec: https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/

We’re happy to run a joint pilot — we estimate ~3 engineer-weeks for a production-ready LangChain/LlamaIndex adapter and ~4–6 engineer-weeks for the in-path SDK work (testing, canaries, and ops hardening). Pricing/marketing to be discussed in the scoping call.

Devon
Lead Integrations Engineer, PromptCraft
devon@promptcraft.ai
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Partnership inquiry — next steps / MAP

Quick summary and next steps for the record:

1) Pilot: Post-hoc telemetry export using OTLP JSON batches. Engineer timeline: Redwood 1 week (event export), PromptCraft 1 week (ingest).
2) Adapter: LangChain + LlamaIndex shim. Timeline: ~3 engineer-weeks (joint). Open-source repo will live under PromptCraft but we’ll provide examples and cross-link docs.
3) In-path SDK: Optional, gated by customer opt-in and SLA. Timeline: 4–6 engineer-weeks if we proceed.
4) Marketing: Co-marketing playbook to be drafted by Marissa.

Action items:
- Marissa: draft pilot MAP + target pilot customers by June 17.
- Jonas: prototype event exporter branch by June 12.
- Devon/Sarah: confirm pilot customer list and sign NDA (if needed).
- Me: schedule a pilot kickoff for June 16 at 10am PT. Calendar invite to follow.

Thanks everyone — excited to move forward.

Soojin Lee
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
